punchline: A friend's remark about unused basketball tickets in a snowstorm went onto a list that grew into behavioral economics.
thirty_sec: As a young economist in Rochester, Richard Thaler kept a list of things people do that economic theory says they shouldn't. A friend, Jeffrey, said that if they had paid full price for tickets to a Buffalo game, they would have driven through the snowstorm. A wine-loving professor would neither buy nor sell a bottle at the going price. Then Thaler read Kahneman and Tversky and saw the oddities as predictable patterns.
